title: HTTPS
body:
HTTPS is [[HTTP]] carried over a connection encrypted by the [[TLS Handshake]]. It provides exactly three guarantees:

- **Confidentiality** — nobody on the backbone routers in between can read the contents.
- **Integrity** — nobody can tamper with the message in transit undetected, because tampering breaks the cryptographic checksum.
- **Authentication** — you're talking to the real server, because a [[Certificate Authority]] signed its certificate and your browser verified that chain of trust.

The common interview trap: the padlock icon only confirms that the connection is encrypted and that the certificate matches the domain being visited. It says nothing whatsoever about whether the site itself is trustworthy — a phishing site can and usually does have a perfectly valid certificate.
